newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES MIXED IN SPECULATIVE MARKET.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES MIXED IN SPECULATIVE MARKET.

text.p: Short-term trading rates on Zimbabwe's money market were quoted mixed on Thursday as players speculated on the direction of rates after the closure of a government stock issue.
The government came into the market last week to float the seven-year issue which market sources say looks set to attract over Z$1 billion.
"People are expecting rates to go up because of a money shortage after the stock issue," one dealer said on Thursday morning.

But he added: "At the same time people have been speculating the treasury bill rate would come down at today's (weekly) tender, due to maturities, and are holding paper at lower rates. It's all a bit mixed at the moment. We will get the real picture after the tender."
Meanwhile, discount houses were trading treasury bills at 18 percent, slightly up from 17.50 percent on Wednesday.

NCD bills maturing after 30, 60 and 90 days were being bought and sold easier at 19 and 18 percent respectively from 19.50 and 18.25 percent, while bankers acceptance bills were quoted steady at 18.25 percent on the buying side but softer at 17.50 from 17.75 percent on the selling side.
Call money added one percentage point to 18 percent in a market which was in surplus of over Z$668 million at settlement.
